newsitem.title: USA: Reverend Jackson calls for Chevron boycott.
newsitem.headline: Reverend Jackson calls for Chevron boycott.

text.p: The Reverend Jesse Jackson wants consumers to boycott Chevron Corp to support of a law suit brought by residents in an area of south Houston.

Jackson told Reuters in an interview on Friday that his Rainbow/Push coalition, an organisation which aims to promote the rights of minorities, was mobilising other organisations to boycott Chevron's products as a result of the pollution of the Kennedy Heights area of Houston.

The suit alleges that oil storage tanks owned by Gulf Oil Co, which was bought by Chevron in 1985, have contaminated land and water in an area inhabited by 3,000 black residents and seeks their relocation and compensation.
"There are birth defects and cancers in the population," Jackson said.
Chevron says it can find no evidence of contamination, despite spending $3.5 million on tests in the area and the storage tanks have not contained oil for some 70 years.
"We have offered to waive our legal defence and appeal rights and go to arbitration, but that was rejected by the plaintiffs' lawyers," a spokesman for Chevron said on Friday.
Jackson's group has bought shares in major oil companies in the U.S. such as Chevron, Shell Oil Co, the U.S. unit of Royal Dutch/Shell, Texaco Inc and Amoco Corp to exert pressure on company boards.
The issue of oil companies' treatment of black employees was highlighted last year when Texaco paid $176 million to settle a lawsuit alleging discrimination.
